**Team Vitality**, or simply **Vitality**, is a French esport club founded in 2013 by Fabien "Neo" Devide, Nicolas Maurer, Corentin "Gotaga" Houssein, and Kevin "BrokyBrawks" Georges.

Team Vitality has teams in ten PC/console esports titles (_[League of Legends](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League\_of\_Legends "League of Legends")_, _[Valorant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valorant "Valorant")_, _[Counter-Strike 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Counter-Strike\_2 "Counter-Strike 2")_, _[Rocket League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocket\_League "Rocket League")_, [_EA FC_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EA_Sports_FC "EA Sports FC"), [_StarCraft II_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/StarCraft_2 "StarCraft 2"), _[Tekken](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tekken "Tekken")_, _[Street Fighter 6](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Street\_Fighter\_6 "Street Fighter 6")_, [_Call of Duty Warzone_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Call_of_Duty:_Warzone_(2020_video_game) "Call of Duty: Warzone (2020 video game)") and _[Teamfight Tactics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teamfight\_Tactics "Teamfight Tactics")_), with several professional teams and content creators from across Europe and [South Korea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Korea "South Korea"). Vitality also has teams in four mobile esports titles (_[Mobile Legends: Bang Bang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mobile\_Legends:\_Bang\_Bang "Mobile Legends: Bang Bang")_, _[Honor of Kings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honor\_of\_Kings "Honor of Kings")_, _[Free Fire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free\_Fire\_(video\_game) "Free Fire (video game)")_ and _[PUBG Mobile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PUBG\_Mobile "PUBG Mobile")_) under the name "Bigetron by Vitality" after they acquired the [Indonesian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indonesia "Indonesia") organization Bigetron Esports in 2025. The organization has previously fielded teams in numerous other titles, including _[Call of Duty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Call\_of\_Duty "Call of Duty")_, [_Call of Duty Mobile_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Call_of_Duty:_Mobile "Call of Duty: Mobile"), [_Fortnite_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fortnite_Battle_Royale "Fortnite Battle Royale"), [_Rainbow Six: Siege_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Clancy's_Rainbow_Six_Siege "Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six Siege"), [_PUBG_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PUBG:_Battlegrounds "PUBG: Battlegrounds"), _[H1Z1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H1Z1 "H1Z1")_, _[Clash Royale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clash\_Royale "Clash Royale")_, _[Street Fighter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Street\_Fighter "Street Fighter")_, _[Formula 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F1\_25 "F1 25")_, _[Hearthstone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hearthstone "Hearthstone")_, _[Gears of War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gears\_of\_War "Gears of War")_ and _[Arena of Valor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arena\_of\_Valor "Arena of Valor")_, as well as previously operating in [India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India "India").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-2)

Since 2019, the organization has made the [Stade de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stade_de_France "Stade de France") its training center, becoming the first resident club of the stadium.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-3)

## _League of Legends_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Team_Vitality&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: League of Legends")]

Team Vitality entered the professional _League of Legends_ on 9 December 2015, after it acquired [Gambit Gaming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gambit_Gaming "Gambit Gaming")'s spot in the [2016 EU LCS Spring Split](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_EU_LCS_Spring "2016 EU LCS Spring").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-Bury-4) The first player signed to the team at the time of the announcement was former [TSM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_SoloMid "Team SoloMid") support [Raymond "kaSing" Tsang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KaSing "KaSing").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-Bury-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-5) Five days later, Vitality announced the rest of their roster, which consisted of top laner [Lucas "Cabochard" Simon-Meslet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabochard "Cabochard"),[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-6) jungler Ilyas "Shook" Hartsema,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-7) mid laner Erlend "Nukeduck" Våtevik Holm,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-8) and kaSing's former teammate, bot laner Petter "Hjarnan" Freyschuss.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-9) For their coaching staff, Vitality signed former Gambit Gaming coach Shaunz.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-10)

### 2016

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Team_Vitality&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: 2016")]

During the 2016 EU LCS Spring Split, Vitality's roster was considered one of the top lineups in the league, finishing in third place with a 13–5 record, behind the surprise first place [G2 Esports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G2_Esports "G2 Esports") and second place [H2k-Gaming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H2k-Gaming "H2k-Gaming"). Cabochard and kaSing were elected to the split's All Pro Team, as the most outstanding players in their positions.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-11) In playoffs, however, they were upset by sixth place [Fnatic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fnatic "Fnatic") and eliminated in the quarterfinals.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-12)

Before the start of the 2016 EU LCS Summer Split, Shook and Hjarnan left the team, the latter for health reasons. Vitality then signed Kim "Mightybear" Min-soo, the former jungler of [Newbee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newbee "Newbee"), and acquired bot laner Park "Police" Hyeong-gi from [Apex Gaming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apex_Gaming "Apex Gaming").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-13)

With the new match format, Vitality failed to live up to prior standards, accruing only three match wins throughout the summer regular season with a 3–9–6 series record. Shook returned four weeks into the season and became the starting jungler once again.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-14) After winning a tiebreaker against [FC Schalke 04](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Schalke_04_Esports "FC Schalke 04 Esports"), Vitality secured seventh place and avoided playing in the relegation series, although they also missed playoffs.

### 2017

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Team_Vitality&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 2017")]

Prior to the start of the competitive season, Vitality again revamped its roster. Bot laner Pierre "Steeelback" Medjaldi was acquired from [Team ROCCAT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_ROCCAT "Team ROCCAT") to replace Police,[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-17) and Ha "Hachani" Seung-chan, a former support for [KT Rolster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KT_Rolster "KT Rolster"), was signed to replace kaSing.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-18) In the jungle, Vitality initially looked toward [Afreeca Freecs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afreeca_Freecs "Afreeca Freecs") jungler LirA, but the deal unexpectedly fell through, as LirA reportedly felt uncomfortable with the move.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-19) Vitality instead ended up signing [Lee "GBM" Chang-seok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GBM_(video_game_player) "GBM (video game player)") as a substitute mid laner,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-20) as well as jungler Charly "Djoko" Guillard of the EU CS team Millenium.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-21) Top laner Adrien "Alderiate" Wils and support Baltat "AoD" Alin-Ciprian were also signed with the team as substitutes.

With the reorganization of the EU LCS regular season format, Vitality was drafted into Group B for the 2017 EU LCS Spring Split, along with [Origen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Origen_(esports) "Origen (esports)"), H2k, [Splyce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Splyce "Splyce"), and the [Unicorns of Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unicorns_of_Love "Unicorns of Love"). After opening the season with a 1–3 record over three weeks, Hachani was benched.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-22) Three days later, GBM moved to the starting mid laner position, while Nukeduck took over the vacant support position. Because of a continuous lack of success, Vitality kept reshuffling their roster around without significant improvement and ended far out of reach of playoff positions in fourth place of the group, only beating Origen twice and the last place team of Group A, [Giants Gaming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giants_Gaming "Giants Gaming").

For the 2017 EU LCS Summer Split, Vitality signed support Oskar "Vander" Bogdan[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-23) and got picked into a nearly identical Group B with the recently promoted Mysterious Monkeys instead of Origen. Despite mild improvements thanks to the roster change, Vitality once again finished fourth in their group.

### 2018

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Team_Vitality&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2018")]

Vitality completely rebuilt their roster around top laner Cabochard going into 2018 and signed veteran jungler Erberk "Gilius" Demir, along with rookies mid laner Daniele "Jiizuke" di Mauro, bot laner Amadeu "Minitroupax" Carvalho, and support Jakub "Jactroll" Skurzyński, who together had won the 2018 Spring Promotion tournament while they were with Giants Gaming.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-24) The new roster surprised many with a 7–1 start to the spring regular season with their explosive playstyle; however, as other teams adapted to their strategies, Vitality began dropping games and finished fourth with a 10–8 record. Vitality ended fourth in playoffs as well after defeating H2k 3–2 in the quarterfinals[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-25) and losing to Fnatic 1–3 in the semifinals and Splyce 2–3 in the third place decider match.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-26)

Following a mediocre 5–5 first half of the 2018 EU LCS Summer Split, Vitality signed veteran jungler Mateusz "Kikis" Szkudlarek after week five, hoping that he could improve the roster with his experience.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-27) Vitality finished the regular season in second place after winning two tiebreaker games against FC Schalke 04 and [G2 Esports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G2_Esports "G2 Esports"). Because of this improvement due to the roster change, Gilius decided to step away from the team as they were performing better with Kikis.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-28) In the semifinals Vitality lost against FC Schalke 04, but later managed to defeat [Misfits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_Gaming "Misfits Gaming") 3–1 in the third place decider match[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-30)—the latter result earned Vitality the second most championship points, qualifying them for the [2018 World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_League_of_Legends_World_Championship "2018 League of Legends World Championship") as Europe's second seed.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-31)

At the 2018 World Championship, Vitality were drawn into Group B along with LCK third seed [Gen.G](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gen.G "Gen.G"), NA LCS third seed [Cloud9](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloud9 "Cloud9") and LPL favourites [Royal Never Give Up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Never_Give_Up "Royal Never Give Up") (RNG). After going 1–2 in the first week, Vitality upset RNG in the second, but still ended third in their group with a 3–3 record, ending their worlds run.

On 20 November 2018, Riot Games announced Team Vitality as one of ten franchise teams of the newly rebranded [_League of Legends_ European Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends_European_Championship "League of Legends European Championship") (LEC).[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-Rand112018-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-Fitch112018-33)

### 2019

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Team_Vitality&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2019")]

For the 2019 LEC Spring Split, Vitality acquired jungler Lee "Mowgli" Jae-ha from LCK team Afreeca Freecs. The team finished the regular season in fifth place with a 10–8 record and later lost 0–3 to Fnatic in the quarterfinals.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-34) Vitality did not make any roster changes going into the 2019 LEC Summer Split and barely clenched a playoff spot after defeating [SK Gaming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SK_Gaming "SK Gaming") in a sixth place tiebreaker match.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-35) In the first round of playoffs Vitality was knocked out by FC Schalke 04, who defeated them 3–1.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-36)

## _Rainbow Six: Siege_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Team_Vitality&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Rainbow Six: Siege")]

Team Vitality first acquired a _Rainbow Six: Siege_ roster on [Xbox One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_One "Xbox One") for the Xbox One Pro League in December 2015, shortly after the game was released. Vitality competed in all three seasons of the Xbox One Pro League and took first in Season Three. Vitality also placed second in the first and only Xbox One Six Invitational in February 2016.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-37) Following this, the Xbox One Pro League shut down and Vitality picked up a PC roster which consisted of Bryan "Elemzje" Tebessi, Julian "Enemy" Blin, Dimitri "Panix" de Longeaux, Jean "RevaN" Prudenti, Valentin "Risze" Liradelfo, and Sami "Stooflex" Smail as coach. Shortly after, the Vitality _Rainbow Six: Siege_ Xbox One team transferred to PC as Vitality. Black with Quentin "Tactiss" Rousselle replacing Arnaud "BiOs" Billaudel a few months later. The original PC team then became known as Vitality.White. Stooflex and Elemzje left Vitality.White later that year in June with Jean-Baptiste "Hansen" Mace replacing Elemzje along with Laurie "Lyloun" Lagier and Julien "Kivvi" Serrier joining as coaches in September 2016.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-:0-38) Vitality.Black then disbanded later in September, allowing Lyloun to join the main team. In February 2018, Valentin "Voy" Cheron replaced Hansen, only weeks before the Six Invitational 2018, the _Rainbow Six: Siege_ world championship, where they placed 13th–16th, the lowest possible placement in the tournament.

On 12 March 2018, Vitality dropped their current roster after disappointing results at the Six Invitational 2018 and acquired the roster of French team Supremacy.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-:3-39) This new roster performed better than the former, placing third in European Pro League Season 7, second in the Coupe de France 2018, and second at Dreamhack Valencia 2018, qualifying for the Six Major Paris 2018. Shortly before Dreamhack Valencia, BiOs returned to Vitality as a coach. At the Six Major Paris 2018, Vitality placed 5th–8th, after defeating both [Team Liquid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Liquid "Team Liquid") and [PET Nora-Rengo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PET_Nora-Rengo "PET Nora-Rengo"), but being eliminated by [Team Secret](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Secret "Team Secret"), the same team they were defeated by at Dreamhack Valencia.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-40) While performing well at offline events, Vitality struggle online and placed seventh in European Pro League Season 8, and lost the relegation match to ENCE. After being relegated to the Challenger League, Adrien "RaFaLe" Rutik and Florian "ZephiR" Perrot along with coach BiOs left to return to Supremacy. Morgan "rxwd" Pacy and David "sNKy" Khalfa would replace them while Lyloun would become the primary coach.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-:1-41)

After performing well in European Challenger League Season 9 during early 2019, Vitality played against long-time rivals Team Secret after losing to MnM Gaming (now Natus Vincere) in a match which determines who goes straight to European Pro League Season 10. Vitality defeated Secret 2–1 and qualified for European Pro League Season 10.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-42) Vitality competed in the Allied Esports Vegas Minor in which they placed 9th–11th after defeating PENTA and Team oNe, but falling to European team [Chaos Esports Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chaos_Esports_Club "Chaos Esports Club") and top North American teams Spacestation Gaming and Rise Nation.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-43) At Dreamhack Valencia 2019, Vitality defeated Korean team [Cloud9](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloud9 "Cloud9") twice and lost to [FaZe Clan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FaZe_Clan "FaZe Clan") in the group stage, and were eliminated in the quarterfinals by Chaos. During the halfway point of European Pro League Season 10, Vitality placed third by defeating top European teams such as [Natus Vincere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natus_Vincere "Natus Vincere") and Chaos. Additionally, Vitality defeated world champions [G2 Esports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G2_Esports "G2 Esports") 7–5 and lost only to Team Empire and [Giants Gaming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giants_Gaming "Giants Gaming"), who were placed first and second at the time respectively.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-44) During the European Six Major Raleigh qualifier, Vitality were favorites to win alongside Chaos. Vitality placed first after defeating teams such as PENTA Sports and BDS Esports, but being disqualified due to disconnecting from the match against ForZe Esports, who went on to win the qualifier and place 3–4th in the event. In the second half of the season, Vitality was still in the running for the Pro League Season 10 Finals, but were effectively eliminated due to losses against G2 and Empire, even though the team later beat Giants without losing a round.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-45)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-46) They placed 5th, just behind Empire and G2, but ahead of Chaos, PENTA, and GiFu Esports. Vitality placed second in the 6 French League 2019, after tying 3 times and only losing twice, against first place [Giants Gaming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giants_Gaming "Giants Gaming").

After season 10 of Pro League, Spark and Quaal were benched and replaced by two time world champion of Daniel "Goga" Mazorra Romero of G2 along with Lucas "Hungry" Reich of PENTA.

Team Vitality announced on 16 March 2021 that they were benching Fabian and Goga, two of the most decorated _Rainbow Six_ players of all time, and the immediate release of Hungry. They were replaced by Kaktus, P4 and Shiinka respectively. Team Vitality also hired ex-Rogue manager Robz. On 16 June 2021, Team Vitality released Fabian from the roster who immediately joined an organisation-less team along with his former teammate, Pengu.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-47)

## _Rocket League_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Team_Vitality&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Rocket League")]

Vitality ventured into the professional _Rocket League_ scene after it acquired the roster of Guess Who on 12 February 2018. The team was renamed **Renault Vitality**, after titular sponsor [Renault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renault "Renault").[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-Bruel5919-48)

Renault Vitality defeated G2 Esports on 23 June 2019 to win Season 7 of the Rocket League Championship Series.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-49) Kyle "Scrub Killa" Robertson was named Worlds MVP.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-50)

On 15 December, during the RLCS Season 8 Finals in Madrid, Renault Vitality was able to reach the final match again. This time they lost to NRG Esports in seven games.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-51)

On 15 January 2020, Vitality announced that they had released Scrub Killa.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-52)

At the same time, the new third player, Alpha54 was announced.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-53)

On 20 June 2021, Vitality won the European RLCS X Championship against Team BDS.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-54)

Vitality signed Victor "Ferra" Francal on 30 March 2022 as their head coach, replacing Mout.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-55)

Following the RLCS 2021–2022 Winter Major, Radosin from GRIDSERVE Resolve was added to the starting roster and Fairy Peak! was moved to the substitute position.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-56)

After the RLCS 2021/2022 season, Kaydop and Fairy Peak were replaced by saizen and zen.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-57)[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-58)

During the RLCS 2022–2023 Winter Regional, Vitality qualified as the 4th seed for the Winter Major which is to be held in San Diego for the first time since the 2021–2022 season.

On 9 July 2023, Team Vitality won the RLCS Spring Major over Team BDS, after winning the EU Open, EU Cup and EU Invitational beforehand. This was the first time any Rocket League team swept all available tournaments for an RLCS split.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-59)[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-60)[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-61) The team would win the World Championship on 13 August against Team BDS once more; this made Team Vitality the first team in RLCS history to win multiple World Championships, as well as extending their RLCS tournament winning streak to 5.

For the 2025 season; Team Vitality announced that Radosin had left the team. Alpha54 was moved to the inactive roster. Monkey Moon and Exotiik were signed on to the team. Kassio replaced Ferra as the team’s coach.

At the Birmingham Major, Team Vitality ended up going 3-0 into the Swiss. At main event, they were defeated at the hands of The Ultimates 4-2 and would later be defeated by Furia 4-3.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-62)

At the Raleigh Major, Vitality also went 3-0 into the Swiss. At main event, they swept NRG Esports 4-0 but were eliminated in the semi finals 4-1 by Dignitas.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-63)[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-64)

At the Esports World Cup Featuring Rocket League, they went on in Group D to beat Spacestation Gaming and Twisted Minds 3-0 to advance to the quarter finals.

In the playoffs, they beat NRG Esports 4-2 to advance to the semi finals where they would painfully lose 4-3 to Geekay Esports and then lose 4-3 in Overtime of the Third Place Match vs Team Falcons.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-65)

At the RLCS World Championship in 2025, they placed 12th after beating Spacestation Gaming 3-2 in a close series but then losing 3-1 to Team Falcons and Ninjas in Pyjamas to end their tournament run.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-66)

During the 2026 offseason, Team Vitality announced M0nkey M00n had left the team, who went on to join Twisted Minds. The coach Kassio retired from the sport. In October 2025, Team Vitality announced the signing of Gaspar “Stizzy” Rosalen from Dignitas and Eversax from Gentle Mates.

## Sim racing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Team_Vitality&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Sim racing")]

On 7 May 2024, Team Vitality announced a partnership with R8G Esports, owned by former [Formula One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula_One "Formula One") driver [Romain Grosjean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romain_Grosjean "Romain Grosjean"), to acquire the latter's ESL R1 slot, with ESL R1 being the main racing league of the then-closed alpha racing simulator _[Rennsport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rennsport "Rennsport")_. Similar to Vitality's entries into _StarCraft II_ and _Tekken_, this opportunity of recruitment may have been funded via the Saudi-operated Esports World Cup Club Support Program, of which Team Vitality is a member.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-advocateeswcprogram-93)[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-advocateeswcprogrammembers-94)

Following their departure, Team Vitality also acquired [_Gran Turismo_ World Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gran_Turismo_World_Series "Gran Turismo World Series") competitors Kaj de Bruin, Antonio Santos, and [Olympic Esports Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_Esports_Series#2023_Olympic_Esports_Week "Olympic Esports Series") Motorsport gold medallist Kylian Drumont.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-96)

## Bigetron by Vitality

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Team_Vitality&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Bigetron by Vitality")]

Team Vitality's first mobile esports venture was with a European _[Arena of Valor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arena\_of\_Valor "Arena of Valor")_ roster that competed in the Valor Series in 2018.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] Their second would be with an all-Indian _[Call of Duty: Mobile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Call\_of\_Duty:\_Mobile "Call of Duty: Mobile")_ team, announced on 26 March 2021.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-97) The _COD: Mobile_ division of Vitality would last until 2025.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

On 13 May 2024, Team Vitality announced that it would enter _Mobile Legends: Bang Bang_ esports by welcoming the former Bigetron Era female roster to its ranks, before signing a European _[Honor of Kings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honor\_of\_Kings "Honor of Kings")_ roster on 12 June. These opportunities of recruitment, as with others in 2024, may have been funded via the Saudi-operated Esports World Cup Club Support Program, of which Team Vitality is a member.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-advocateeswcprogram-93)[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-advocateeswcprogrammembers-94) The _Honor of Kings_ roster in question would be acquired by [OG Esports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OG_(esports) "OG (esports)") in April 2025.

On 15 May 2025, Vitality announced that they would acquire the [Indonesian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indonesia "Indonesia") organization Bigetron Esports, as well as its divisions, with their mobile games branch renamed to "Bigetron by Vitality". With the Bigetron acquisition, Vitality added a male _Mobile Legends: Bang Bang_ roster that competes in the [MPL Indonesia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MPL_Indonesia "MPL Indonesia"), a male academy roster which competes in the MDL Indonesia, a new _Honor of Kings_ roster competing in the Indonesian Kings Laga, as well as _[PUBG Mobile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PUBG\_Mobile "PUBG Mobile")_ and _[Free Fire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free\_Fire\_(video\_game) "Free Fire (video game)")_ rosters.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-98)

### V.Hive

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Team_Vitality&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: V.Hive")]

Vitality has its headquarters at V.Hive, located [Boulevard de Sébastopol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boulevard_de_S%C3%A9bastopol "Boulevard de Sébastopol") in [Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris "Paris"), since November 2019.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-99) This place of 1000m² is also the first physical link between the club and its fans, since a part is open to the public with shop, meeting place and [cybercafé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cybercaf%C3%A9 "Cybercafé"). In addition to this first venue open to the public, Vitality plans to develop this concept in [Lyon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyon "Lyon"), [Marseille](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marseille "Marseille"), [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London") or [Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin "Berlin").

### Vitality Performance Center

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Team_Vitality&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Vitality Performance Center")]

Since 2019, Vitality has also invested in the [Stade de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stade_de_France "Stade de France") where its training centre, named Vitality Performance Center, is established, in a desire to professionalize its teams at the highest level.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-100) The team _[FIFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA\_(video\_game\_series) "FIFA (video game series)")_ settled there in September 2019, then two others, the team _[Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six Siege](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom\_Clancy's\_Rainbow\_Six\_Siege "Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six Siege")_ replaced today by the team _[Rocket League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocket\_League "Rocket League")_ and the academic team of _[League of Legends](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League\_of\_Legends "League of Legends")_ Vitality.Bee playing in LFL in the French championship, will follow in 2020. Finally, since 2023, the women's team of _League of Legends_ uses from time to time the facilities to realize weeks of training at the highest level. Vitality also aims in the medium term to build an arena from 1500 to 2000 places inside the [Stade de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stade_de_France "Stade de France") to play its home matches.

### Gaming House Berlin

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Team_Vitality&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Gaming House Berlin")]

As part of their respective participation in the [LEC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends_Championship_Series "League of Legends Championship Series") and [Valorant Champions Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valorant_Champions_Tour "Valorant Champions Tour"), Vitality's main team on _[League of Legends](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League\_of\_Legends "League of Legends")_ and the [Valorant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valorant "Valorant") train in a gaming house located in [Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin "Berlin"). Joined by the [Counter-Strike 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Counter-Strike_2 "Counter-Strike 2") team since 2018, these 3 teams train in a healthy environment optimized to perform at the highest European and global levels.

### Gaming House India

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Team_Vitality&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Gaming House India")]

Since November 2018 and the fundraising with Indian billionaire Tej Kohli,[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-101) Vitality is present on the game _[Call of Duty: Mobile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Call\_of\_Duty:\_Mobile "Call of Duty: Mobile")_, in order to bring players together and allow them to play at the highest level, the organization has invested in a gaming house in [Navi Mumbai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navi_Mumbai "Navi Mumbai").

The Indian division had also acquired a [Free Fire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_Fire_(video_game) "Free Fire (video game)") team, initially announcing Fab Indro as the coach of their roster on 28 January 2022[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-102) and parted ways on 6 March 2023.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-103)

### Gaming House Jakarta

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Team_Vitality&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Gaming House Jakarta")]

As part of the participation in the Esports World Cup, and the arrival on several new games including [Mobile Legends: Bang Bang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mobile_Legends:_Bang_Bang "Mobile Legends: Bang Bang"), the club invests in a gaming house located in [Jakarta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jakarta "Jakarta"), Indonesia to ensure a healthy and optimized environment for performance.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-104)

**Team Vitality**, or simply **Vitality**, is a French esport club founded in 2013 by Fabien "Neo" Devide, Nicolas Maurer, Corentin "Gotaga" Houssein, and Kevin "BrokyBrawks" Georges.

Team Vitality has teams in ten PC/console esports titles (_[League of Legends](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League\_of\_Legends "League of Legends")_, _[Valorant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valorant "Valorant")_, _[Counter-Strike 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Counter-Strike\_2 "Counter-Strike 2")_, _[Rocket League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocket\_League "Rocket League")_, [_EA FC_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EA_Sports_FC "EA Sports FC"), [_StarCraft II_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/StarCraft_2 "StarCraft 2"), _[Tekken](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tekken "Tekken")_, _[Street Fighter 6](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Street\_Fighter\_6 "Street Fighter 6")_, [_Call of Duty Warzone_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Call_of_Duty:_Warzone_(2020_video_game) "Call of Duty: Warzone (2020 video game)") and _[Teamfight Tactics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teamfight\_Tactics "Teamfight Tactics")_), with several professional teams and content creators from across Europe and [South Korea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Korea "South Korea"). Vitality also has teams in four mobile esports titles (_[Mobile Legends: Bang Bang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mobile\_Legends:\_Bang\_Bang "Mobile Legends: Bang Bang")_, _[Honor of Kings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honor\_of\_Kings "Honor of Kings")_, _[Free Fire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free\_Fire\_(video\_game) "Free Fire (video game)")_ and _[PUBG Mobile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PUBG\_Mobile "PUBG Mobile")_) under the name "Bigetron by Vitality" after they acquired the [Indonesian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indonesia "Indonesia") organization Bigetron Esports in 2025. The organization has previously fielded teams in numerous other titles, including _[Call of Duty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Call\_of\_Duty "Call of Duty")_, [_Call of Duty Mobile_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Call_of_Duty:_Mobile "Call of Duty: Mobile"), [_Fortnite_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fortnite_Battle_Royale "Fortnite Battle Royale"), [_Rainbow Six: Siege_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Clancy's_Rainbow_Six_Siege "Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six Siege"), [_PUBG_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PUBG:_Battlegrounds "PUBG: Battlegrounds"), _[H1Z1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H1Z1 "H1Z1")_, _[Clash Royale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clash\_Royale "Clash Royale")_, _[Street Fighter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Street\_Fighter "Street Fighter")_, _[Formula 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F1\_25 "F1 25")_, _[Hearthstone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hearthstone "Hearthstone")_, _[Gears of War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gears\_of\_War "Gears of War")_ and _[Arena of Valor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arena\_of\_Valor "Arena of Valor")_, as well as previously operating in [India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India "India").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-2)

Since 2019, the organization has made the [Stade de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stade_de_France "Stade de France") its training center, becoming the first resident club of the stadium.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-3)

## _League of Legends_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Team_Vitality&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: League of Legends")]

Team Vitality entered the professional _League of Legends_ on 9 December 2015, after it acquired [Gambit Gaming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gambit_Gaming "Gambit Gaming")'s spot in the [2016 EU LCS Spring Split](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_EU_LCS_Spring "2016 EU LCS Spring").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-Bury-4) The first player signed to the team at the time of the announcement was former [TSM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_SoloMid "Team SoloMid") support [Raymond "kaSing" Tsang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KaSing "KaSing").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-Bury-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-5) Five days later, Vitality announced the rest of their roster, which consisted of top laner [Lucas "Cabochard" Simon-Meslet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabochard "Cabochard"),[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-6) jungler Ilyas "Shook" Hartsema,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-7) mid laner Erlend "Nukeduck" Våtevik Holm,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-8) and kaSing's former teammate, bot laner Petter "Hjarnan" Freyschuss.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-9) For their coaching staff, Vitality signed former Gambit Gaming coach Shaunz.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-10)

### 2016

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Team_Vitality&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: 2016")]

During the 2016 EU LCS Spring Split, Vitality's roster was considered one of the top lineups in the league, finishing in third place with a 13–5 record, behind the surprise first place [G2 Esports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G2_Esports "G2 Esports") and second place [H2k-Gaming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H2k-Gaming "H2k-Gaming"). Cabochard and kaSing were elected to the split's All Pro Team, as the most outstanding players in their positions.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-11) In playoffs, however, they were upset by sixth place [Fnatic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fnatic "Fnatic") and eliminated in the quarterfinals.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-12)

Before the start of the 2016 EU LCS Summer Split, Shook and Hjarnan left the team, the latter for health reasons. Vitality then signed Kim "Mightybear" Min-soo, the former jungler of [Newbee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newbee "Newbee"), and acquired bot laner Park "Police" Hyeong-gi from [Apex Gaming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apex_Gaming "Apex Gaming").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-13)

With the new match format, Vitality failed to live up to prior standards, accruing only three match wins throughout the summer regular season with a 3–9–6 series record. Shook returned four weeks into the season and became the starting jungler once again.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-14) After winning a tiebreaker against [FC Schalke 04](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Schalke_04_Esports "FC Schalke 04 Esports"), Vitality secured seventh place and avoided playing in the relegation series, although they also missed playoffs.

### 2017

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Team_Vitality&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 2017")]

Prior to the start of the competitive season, Vitality again revamped its roster. Bot laner Pierre "Steeelback" Medjaldi was acquired from [Team ROCCAT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_ROCCAT "Team ROCCAT") to replace Police,[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-17) and Ha "Hachani" Seung-chan, a former support for [KT Rolster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KT_Rolster "KT Rolster"), was signed to replace kaSing.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-18) In the jungle, Vitality initially looked toward [Afreeca Freecs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afreeca_Freecs "Afreeca Freecs") jungler LirA, but the deal unexpectedly fell through, as LirA reportedly felt uncomfortable with the move.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-19) Vitality instead ended up signing [Lee "GBM" Chang-seok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GBM_(video_game_player) "GBM (video game player)") as a substitute mid laner,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-20) as well as jungler Charly "Djoko" Guillard of the EU CS team Millenium.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-21) Top laner Adrien "Alderiate" Wils and support Baltat "AoD" Alin-Ciprian were also signed with the team as substitutes.

With the reorganization of the EU LCS regular season format, Vitality was drafted into Group B for the 2017 EU LCS Spring Split, along with [Origen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Origen_(esports) "Origen (esports)"), H2k, [Splyce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Splyce "Splyce"), and the [Unicorns of Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unicorns_of_Love "Unicorns of Love"). After opening the season with a 1–3 record over three weeks, Hachani was benched.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-22) Three days later, GBM moved to the starting mid laner position, while Nukeduck took over the vacant support position. Because of a continuous lack of success, Vitality kept reshuffling their roster around without significant improvement and ended far out of reach of playoff positions in fourth place of the group, only beating Origen twice and the last place team of Group A, [Giants Gaming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giants_Gaming "Giants Gaming").

For the 2017 EU LCS Summer Split, Vitality signed support Oskar "Vander" Bogdan[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-23) and got picked into a nearly identical Group B with the recently promoted Mysterious Monkeys instead of Origen. Despite mild improvements thanks to the roster change, Vitality once again finished fourth in their group.

### 2018

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Team_Vitality&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2018")]

Vitality completely rebuilt their roster around top laner Cabochard going into 2018 and signed veteran jungler Erberk "Gilius" Demir, along with rookies mid laner Daniele "Jiizuke" di Mauro, bot laner Amadeu "Minitroupax" Carvalho, and support Jakub "Jactroll" Skurzyński, who together had won the 2018 Spring Promotion tournament while they were with Giants Gaming.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-24) The new roster surprised many with a 7–1 start to the spring regular season with their explosive playstyle; however, as other teams adapted to their strategies, Vitality began dropping games and finished fourth with a 10–8 record. Vitality ended fourth in playoffs as well after defeating H2k 3–2 in the quarterfinals[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-25) and losing to Fnatic 1–3 in the semifinals and Splyce 2–3 in the third place decider match.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-26)

Following a mediocre 5–5 first half of the 2018 EU LCS Summer Split, Vitality signed veteran jungler Mateusz "Kikis" Szkudlarek after week five, hoping that he could improve the roster with his experience.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-27) Vitality finished the regular season in second place after winning two tiebreaker games against FC Schalke 04 and [G2 Esports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G2_Esports "G2 Esports"). Because of this improvement due to the roster change, Gilius decided to step away from the team as they were performing better with Kikis.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-28) In the semifinals Vitality lost against FC Schalke 04, but later managed to defeat [Misfits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_Gaming "Misfits Gaming") 3–1 in the third place decider match[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-30)—the latter result earned Vitality the second most championship points, qualifying them for the [2018 World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_League_of_Legends_World_Championship "2018 League of Legends World Championship") as Europe's second seed.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-31)

At the 2018 World Championship, Vitality were drawn into Group B along with LCK third seed [Gen.G](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gen.G "Gen.G"), NA LCS third seed [Cloud9](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloud9 "Cloud9") and LPL favourites [Royal Never Give Up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Never_Give_Up "Royal Never Give Up") (RNG). After going 1–2 in the first week, Vitality upset RNG in the second, but still ended third in their group with a 3–3 record, ending their worlds run.

On 20 November 2018, Riot Games announced Team Vitality as one of ten franchise teams of the newly rebranded [_League of Legends_ European Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends_European_Championship "League of Legends European Championship") (LEC).[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-Rand112018-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-Fitch112018-33)

### 2019

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Team_Vitality&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2019")]

For the 2019 LEC Spring Split, Vitality acquired jungler Lee "Mowgli" Jae-ha from LCK team Afreeca Freecs. The team finished the regular season in fifth place with a 10–8 record and later lost 0–3 to Fnatic in the quarterfinals.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-34) Vitality did not make any roster changes going into the 2019 LEC Summer Split and barely clenched a playoff spot after defeating [SK Gaming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SK_Gaming "SK Gaming") in a sixth place tiebreaker match.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-35) In the first round of playoffs Vitality was knocked out by FC Schalke 04, who defeated them 3–1.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-36)

## _Rainbow Six: Siege_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Team_Vitality&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Rainbow Six: Siege")]

Team Vitality first acquired a _Rainbow Six: Siege_ roster on [Xbox One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_One "Xbox One") for the Xbox One Pro League in December 2015, shortly after the game was released. Vitality competed in all three seasons of the Xbox One Pro League and took first in Season Three. Vitality also placed second in the first and only Xbox One Six Invitational in February 2016.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-37) Following this, the Xbox One Pro League shut down and Vitality picked up a PC roster which consisted of Bryan "Elemzje" Tebessi, Julian "Enemy" Blin, Dimitri "Panix" de Longeaux, Jean "RevaN" Prudenti, Valentin "Risze" Liradelfo, and Sami "Stooflex" Smail as coach. Shortly after, the Vitality _Rainbow Six: Siege_ Xbox One team transferred to PC as Vitality. Black with Quentin "Tactiss" Rousselle replacing Arnaud "BiOs" Billaudel a few months later. The original PC team then became known as Vitality.White. Stooflex and Elemzje left Vitality.White later that year in June with Jean-Baptiste "Hansen" Mace replacing Elemzje along with Laurie "Lyloun" Lagier and Julien "Kivvi" Serrier joining as coaches in September 2016.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-:0-38) Vitality.Black then disbanded later in September, allowing Lyloun to join the main team. In February 2018, Valentin "Voy" Cheron replaced Hansen, only weeks before the Six Invitational 2018, the _Rainbow Six: Siege_ world championship, where they placed 13th–16th, the lowest possible placement in the tournament.

On 12 March 2018, Vitality dropped their current roster after disappointing results at the Six Invitational 2018 and acquired the roster of French team Supremacy.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-:3-39) This new roster performed better than the former, placing third in European Pro League Season 7, second in the Coupe de France 2018, and second at Dreamhack Valencia 2018, qualifying for the Six Major Paris 2018. Shortly before Dreamhack Valencia, BiOs returned to Vitality as a coach. At the Six Major Paris 2018, Vitality placed 5th–8th, after defeating both [Team Liquid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Liquid "Team Liquid") and [PET Nora-Rengo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PET_Nora-Rengo "PET Nora-Rengo"), but being eliminated by [Team Secret](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Secret "Team Secret"), the same team they were defeated by at Dreamhack Valencia.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-40) While performing well at offline events, Vitality struggle online and placed seventh in European Pro League Season 8, and lost the relegation match to ENCE. After being relegated to the Challenger League, Adrien "RaFaLe" Rutik and Florian "ZephiR" Perrot along with coach BiOs left to return to Supremacy. Morgan "rxwd" Pacy and David "sNKy" Khalfa would replace them while Lyloun would become the primary coach.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-:1-41)

After performing well in European Challenger League Season 9 during early 2019, Vitality played against long-time rivals Team Secret after losing to MnM Gaming (now Natus Vincere) in a match which determines who goes straight to European Pro League Season 10. Vitality defeated Secret 2–1 and qualified for European Pro League Season 10.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-42) Vitality competed in the Allied Esports Vegas Minor in which they placed 9th–11th after defeating PENTA and Team oNe, but falling to European team [Chaos Esports Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chaos_Esports_Club "Chaos Esports Club") and top North American teams Spacestation Gaming and Rise Nation.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-43) At Dreamhack Valencia 2019, Vitality defeated Korean team [Cloud9](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloud9 "Cloud9") twice and lost to [FaZe Clan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FaZe_Clan "FaZe Clan") in the group stage, and were eliminated in the quarterfinals by Chaos. During the halfway point of European Pro League Season 10, Vitality placed third by defeating top European teams such as [Natus Vincere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natus_Vincere "Natus Vincere") and Chaos. Additionally, Vitality defeated world champions [G2 Esports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G2_Esports "G2 Esports") 7–5 and lost only to Team Empire and [Giants Gaming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giants_Gaming "Giants Gaming"), who were placed first and second at the time respectively.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-44) During the European Six Major Raleigh qualifier, Vitality were favorites to win alongside Chaos. Vitality placed first after defeating teams such as PENTA Sports and BDS Esports, but being disqualified due to disconnecting from the match against ForZe Esports, who went on to win the qualifier and place 3–4th in the event. In the second half of the season, Vitality was still in the running for the Pro League Season 10 Finals, but were effectively eliminated due to losses against G2 and Empire, even though the team later beat Giants without losing a round.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-45)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-46) They placed 5th, just behind Empire and G2, but ahead of Chaos, PENTA, and GiFu Esports. Vitality placed second in the 6 French League 2019, after tying 3 times and only losing twice, against first place [Giants Gaming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giants_Gaming "Giants Gaming").

After season 10 of Pro League, Spark and Quaal were benched and replaced by two time world champion of Daniel "Goga" Mazorra Romero of G2 along with Lucas "Hungry" Reich of PENTA.

Team Vitality announced on 16 March 2021 that they were benching Fabian and Goga, two of the most decorated _Rainbow Six_ players of all time, and the immediate release of Hungry. They were replaced by Kaktus, P4 and Shiinka respectively. Team Vitality also hired ex-Rogue manager Robz. On 16 June 2021, Team Vitality released Fabian from the roster who immediately joined an organisation-less team along with his former teammate, Pengu.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-47)

## _Rocket League_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Team_Vitality&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Rocket League")]

Vitality ventured into the professional _Rocket League_ scene after it acquired the roster of Guess Who on 12 February 2018. The team was renamed **Renault Vitality**, after titular sponsor [Renault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renault "Renault").[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-Bruel5919-48)

Renault Vitality defeated G2 Esports on 23 June 2019 to win Season 7 of the Rocket League Championship Series.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-49) Kyle "Scrub Killa" Robertson was named Worlds MVP.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-50)

On 15 December, during the RLCS Season 8 Finals in Madrid, Renault Vitality was able to reach the final match again. This time they lost to NRG Esports in seven games.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-51)

On 15 January 2020, Vitality announced that they had released Scrub Killa.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-52)

At the same time, the new third player, Alpha54 was announced.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-53)

On 20 June 2021, Vitality won the European RLCS X Championship against Team BDS.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-54)

Vitality signed Victor "Ferra" Francal on 30 March 2022 as their head coach, replacing Mout.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-55)

Following the RLCS 2021–2022 Winter Major, Radosin from GRIDSERVE Resolve was added to the starting roster and Fairy Peak! was moved to the substitute position.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-56)

After the RLCS 2021/2022 season, Kaydop and Fairy Peak were replaced by saizen and zen.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-57)[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-58)

During the RLCS 2022–2023 Winter Regional, Vitality qualified as the 4th seed for the Winter Major which is to be held in San Diego for the first time since the 2021–2022 season.

On 9 July 2023, Team Vitality won the RLCS Spring Major over Team BDS, after winning the EU Open, EU Cup and EU Invitational beforehand. This was the first time any Rocket League team swept all available tournaments for an RLCS split.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-59)[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-60)[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-61) The team would win the World Championship on 13 August against Team BDS once more; this made Team Vitality the first team in RLCS history to win multiple World Championships, as well as extending their RLCS tournament winning streak to 5.

For the 2025 season; Team Vitality announced that Radosin had left the team. Alpha54 was moved to the inactive roster. Monkey Moon and Exotiik were signed on to the team. Kassio replaced Ferra as the team’s coach.

At the Birmingham Major, Team Vitality ended up going 3-0 into the Swiss. At main event, they were defeated at the hands of The Ultimates 4-2 and would later be defeated by Furia 4-3.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-62)

At the Raleigh Major, Vitality also went 3-0 into the Swiss. At main event, they swept NRG Esports 4-0 but were eliminated in the semi finals 4-1 by Dignitas.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-63)[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-64)

At the Esports World Cup Featuring Rocket League, they went on in Group D to beat Spacestation Gaming and Twisted Minds 3-0 to advance to the quarter finals.

In the playoffs, they beat NRG Esports 4-2 to advance to the semi finals where they would painfully lose 4-3 to Geekay Esports and then lose 4-3 in Overtime of the Third Place Match vs Team Falcons.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-65)

At the RLCS World Championship in 2025, they placed 12th after beating Spacestation Gaming 3-2 in a close series but then losing 3-1 to Team Falcons and Ninjas in Pyjamas to end their tournament run.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-66)

During the 2026 offseason, Team Vitality announced M0nkey M00n had left the team, who went on to join Twisted Minds. The coach Kassio retired from the sport. In October 2025, Team Vitality announced the signing of Gaspar “Stizzy” Rosalen from Dignitas and Eversax from Gentle Mates.

## Sim racing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Team_Vitality&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Sim racing")]

On 7 May 2024, Team Vitality announced a partnership with R8G Esports, owned by former [Formula One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula_One "Formula One") driver [Romain Grosjean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romain_Grosjean "Romain Grosjean"), to acquire the latter's ESL R1 slot, with ESL R1 being the main racing league of the then-closed alpha racing simulator _[Rennsport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rennsport "Rennsport")_. Similar to Vitality's entries into _StarCraft II_ and _Tekken_, this opportunity of recruitment may have been funded via the Saudi-operated Esports World Cup Club Support Program, of which Team Vitality is a member.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-advocateeswcprogram-93)[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-advocateeswcprogrammembers-94)

The team later departed from R1 and, in turn, the _Rennsport_ competitive scene in 2026, but reaffirmed their commitments to sim racing, retaining their players from the series and focusing on other racing game platforms and competitions. Following their departure, Team Vitality also acquired [_Gran Turismo_ World Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gran_Turismo_World_Series "Gran Turismo World Series") competitors Kaj de Bruin, Antonio Santos, and [Olympic Esports Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_Esports_Series#2023_Olympic_Esports_Week "Olympic Esports Series") Motorsport gold medallist Kylian Drumont.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-96)

## Bigetron by Vitality

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Team_Vitality&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Bigetron by Vitality")]

Team Vitality's first mobile esports venture was with a European _[Arena of Valor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arena\_of\_Valor "Arena of Valor")_ roster that competed in the Valor Series in 2018.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] Their second would be with an all-Indian _[Call of Duty: Mobile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Call\_of\_Duty:\_Mobile "Call of Duty: Mobile")_ team, announced on 26 March 2021.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-97) The _COD: Mobile_ division of Vitality would last until 2025.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

On 13 May 2024, Team Vitality announced that it would enter _Mobile Legends: Bang Bang_ esports by welcoming the former Bigetron Era female roster to its ranks, before signing a European _[Honor of Kings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honor\_of\_Kings "Honor of Kings")_ roster on 12 June. These opportunities of recruitment, as with others in 2024, may have been funded via the Saudi-operated Esports World Cup Club Support Program, of which Team Vitality is a member.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-advocateeswcprogram-93)[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-advocateeswcprogrammembers-94) The _Honor of Kings_ roster in question would be acquired by [OG Esports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OG_(esports) "OG (esports)") in April 2025.

On 15 May 2025, Vitality announced that they would acquire the [Indonesian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indonesia "Indonesia") organization Bigetron Esports, as well as its divisions, with their mobile games branch renamed to "Bigetron by Vitality". With the Bigetron acquisition, Vitality added a male _Mobile Legends: Bang Bang_ roster that competes in the [MPL Indonesia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MPL_Indonesia "MPL Indonesia"), a male academy roster which competes in the MDL Indonesia, a new _Honor of Kings_ roster competing in the Indonesian Kings Laga, as well as _[PUBG Mobile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PUBG\_Mobile "PUBG Mobile")_ and _[Free Fire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free\_Fire\_(video\_game) "Free Fire (video game)")_ rosters.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-98)

### V.Hive

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Team_Vitality&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: V.Hive")]

Vitality has its headquarters at V.Hive, located [Boulevard de Sébastopol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boulevard_de_S%C3%A9bastopol "Boulevard de Sébastopol") in [Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris "Paris"), since November 2019.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-99) This place of 1000m² is also the first physical link between the club and its fans, since a part is open to the public with shop, meeting place and [cybercafé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cybercaf%C3%A9 "Cybercafé"). In addition to this first venue open to the public, Vitality plans to develop this concept in [Lyon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyon "Lyon"), [Marseille](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marseille "Marseille"), [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London") or [Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin "Berlin").

### Vitality Performance Center

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Team_Vitality&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Vitality Performance Center")]

Since 2019, Vitality has also invested in the [Stade de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stade_de_France "Stade de France") where its training centre, named Vitality Performance Center, is established, in a desire to professionalize its teams at the highest level.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-100) The team _[FIFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA\_(video\_game\_series) "FIFA (video game series)")_ settled there in September 2019, then two others, the team _[Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six Siege](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom\_Clancy's\_Rainbow\_Six\_Siege "Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six Siege")_ replaced today by the team _[Rocket League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocket\_League "Rocket League")_ and the academic team of _[League of Legends](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League\_of\_Legends "League of Legends")_ Vitality.Bee playing in LFL in the French championship, will follow in 2020. Finally, since 2023, the women's team of _League of Legends_ uses from time to time the facilities to realize weeks of training at the highest level. Vitality also aims in the medium term to build an arena from 1500 to 2000 places inside the [Stade de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stade_de_France "Stade de France") to play its home matches.

### Gaming House Berlin

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Team_Vitality&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Gaming House Berlin")]

As part of their respective participation in the [LEC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Legends_Championship_Series "League of Legends Championship Series") and [Valorant Champions Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valorant_Champions_Tour "Valorant Champions Tour"), Vitality's main team on _[League of Legends](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League\_of\_Legends "League of Legends")_ and the [Valorant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valorant "Valorant") train in a gaming house located in [Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin "Berlin"). Joined by the [Counter-Strike 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Counter-Strike_2 "Counter-Strike 2") team since 2018, these 3 teams train in a healthy environment optimized to perform at the highest European and global levels.

### Gaming House India

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Team_Vitality&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Gaming House India")]

Since November 2018 and the fundraising with Indian billionaire Tej Kohli,[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-101) Vitality is present on the game _[Call of Duty: Mobile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Call\_of\_Duty:\_Mobile "Call of Duty: Mobile")_, in order to bring players together and allow them to play at the highest level, the organization has invested in a gaming house in [Navi Mumbai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navi_Mumbai "Navi Mumbai").

The Indian division had also acquired a [Free Fire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_Fire_(video_game) "Free Fire (video game)") team, initially announcing Fab Indro as the coach of their roster on 28 January 2022[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-102) and parted ways on 6 March 2023.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-103)

### Gaming House Jakarta

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Team_Vitality&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Gaming House Jakarta")]

As part of the participation in the Esports World Cup, and the arrival on several new games including [Mobile Legends: Bang Bang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mobile_Legends:_Bang_Bang "Mobile Legends: Bang Bang"), the club invests in a gaming house located in [Jakarta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jakarta "Jakarta"), Indonesia to ensure a healthy and optimized environment for performance.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Vitality#cite_note-104)

The **Rocket League Championship Series** (**RLCS**) is an annual _[Rocket League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocket\_League "Rocket League")_[esports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Esports "Esports") tournament series produced by Blast ApS and endorsed by [Psyonix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psyonix "Psyonix"), the game's developer. It consists of two online qualification splits in several regions, with teams earning points towards qualifying for midseason tournaments known as Majors and the Rocket League World Championship, both of which are held as [LAN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_area_network "Local area network") events worldwide.

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rocket_League_Championship_Series&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

Psyonix had observed the popularity of _Rocket League_ matches on [Twitch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twitch_(service) "Twitch (service)") and other [live streaming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_streaming "Live streaming") platforms like [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube") by early 2016 and were looking to use the game more in Esports.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocket_League_Championship_Series#cite_note-:0-1) In March 2016, Psyonix announced the first Rocket League Championship Series; the finals took place in June 2016 with a US$55,000 prize pool, and was won by iBUYPOWER Cosmic.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocket_League_Championship_Series#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocket_League_Championship_Series#cite_note-3) The second season of the championship series took place in December 2016 with a $125,000 prize pool, and was won by FlipSid3 Tactics.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocket_League_Championship_Series#cite_note-4) A third series began in March 2017, with the $300,000 prize pool finals taking place three months later. In this season, two teams from the oceanic region were also invited to compete.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocket_League_Championship_Series#cite_note-5)

A second division, the Rocket League Rival Series (RLRS), was added in Season 4. The two teams finishing at the bottom of the RLCS and the two teams finishing at the top of the RLRS for each region play each other in a promotion tournament at the end of the season to determine if teams are promoted or relegated. At the advent of Season 5 in June 2018, Psyonix organised and managed the event alone. Previous to this, they partnered with Twitch. Season 6 started in September 2018 and featured a $1,000,000 prize pool.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocket_League_Championship_Series#cite_note-6) For Season 7, Psyonix introduced South America as a new region.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocket_League_Championship_Series#cite_note-7) Season 8 took place in December 2019. The Season 9 championship was cancelled due to the COVID-19 pandemic, with winners of the regional championships being considered the champions.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocket_League_Championship_Series#cite_note-8) In July 2020, Psyonix announced a new format for the tenth season of RLCS, known as RLCS X. This format did away with league play and the RLRS in favor of teams earning points through three regional splits, all culminating in three seasonal majors.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocket_League_Championship_Series#cite_note-9)

The 2021–22 season began in October 2021, bringing in four new regions (Middle East and North Africa, Asia Pacific North, Asia Pacific South, and Sub-Saharan Africa), a more reliable circuit similar to Season X, and a $6 million prize pool. The new circuit consisted of 3 splits, containing 3 regionals and 1 international LAN major each, culminating in a World Championship to finish the season. The Majors were won by Team BDS, [G2 Esports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G2_Esports "G2 Esports") and [Moist Esports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moist_Esports "Moist Esports"). The season was won by Team BDS.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocket_League_Championship_Series#cite_note-10)

For the 2022–23 season Asia Pacific North and Asia Pacific South were combined into a single region with point totals being lowered and each regional event being called the Open, Cup and invitational. The Majors were won by [Gen.G](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gen.G "Gen.G"), [Karmine Corp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karmine_Corp "Karmine Corp") and Team Vitality, the latter of which would go on to win the World Championship.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocket_League_Championship_Series#cite_note-11)

Unlike the past two seasons, there was a considerably longer offseason after 2022–23 accompanying the removal of one of the splits, meaning that the 13th season of the RLCS wouldn't begin until January 26, 2024.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocket_League_Championship_Series#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocket_League_Championship_Series#cite_note-13) The 2024 season saw the removal of the Open, Cup and Invitational system for each region in favor of three new open qualifying stages, those being a double-elimination qualifying bracket, a [Swiss-system tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swiss-system_tournament "Swiss-system tournament") featuring the top 16 from open qualifying and a knockout stage featuring the top 8 from the Swiss stage. This open qualifying cycle is repeated three times per split, awarding RLCS points after each stage, before the top teams in RLCS points in each region from those stages advance to that split's Major, which features the Swiss and knockout stages from open qualifying and award additional points. The combined standings decides who advances to the World Championship, which was reduced from 24 to 16 teams in the process using the same format as the Majors.

On January 4, 2024, it was announced that Blast ApS, a tournament organizer known for the [Blast Premier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blast_Premier "Blast Premier") circuit in _[Counter-Strike](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Counter-Strike "Counter-Strike")_ as well as organizing the esports circuit for _[Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six Siege](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom\_Clancy's\_Rainbow\_Six\_Siege "Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six Siege")_, would take over from Psyonix as organizer for the RLCS in 2024, having previously run the [_Fortnite_ Championship Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fortnite_Championship_Series "Fortnite Championship Series") (previously run by Psyonix's parent company [Epic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epic_Games "Epic Games")) since 2022.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocket_League_Championship_Series#cite_note-14)

The first major of the RLCS 2024 season was won by Gentlemates Alpine, with the second won by G2 Stride. The season was won by Team BDS. Towards the end of the RLCS 2024 World Championship, it was announced that RLCS would return for the 2025 season in January, with a total prize pool of $5,000,000, the addition of a 1v1 tournament, and changes to the 3v3 tournament which include the addition of a last chance open qualifiers tournament between Major 2 and the World Championship, and expanding the World Championship to 20 teams.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocket_League_Championship_Series#cite_note-15)

The 2025 season uses 2 Swiss groups, 16 teams in each. Top 8 of each group advance to the GSL stage. 2 groups of 8, 4 advance to the hybrid elimination bracket. This format is used for Opens and the World Championship, but Worlds doesn't use the Swiss groups and uses a GSL bracket for the Play-ins. Before the Swiss groups, there is a double elimination bracket and top 32 qualify for the Swiss groups (24 in Open 2, 3, 5 and 6 as top 8 of the last Open automatically qualify for the Swiss groups). Majors use a 16 team Swiss stage, in which top 8 qualify for the hybrid elimination bracket.

The first major of the season was won by Karmine Corp. The major also debuted the RLCS 1v1 event, which was won by France's Axel "Mawkzy" Timone, defeating Brazil's Yan "yanxnz" Xisto Nolasco 4–3. Mawkzy will compete at the RLCS World Championship at Lyon-Décines in September.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocket_League_Championship_Series#cite_note-16) The second major of the season was won by Team Falcons and marked the Middle East's first RLCS international title since their introduction to the league in 2021.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocket_League_Championship_Series#cite_note-17) The Middle East is, to date, the only region outside North America or Europe that have won an RLCS international event. The second major's RLCS 1v1 final also saw Saudi Arabia's Hisham "Nwpo" Alqadi defeat Brazil's João "diaz" Henrique 4–1 to qualify for the 1v1 World Championship, where he faced Mawkzy for the title of RLCS's first 1v1 World Champion, and won 4–1 in the Grand Final.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocket_League_Championship_Series#cite_note-18) Also in the 2025 World Championship was the 3v3 event, where NRG Esports won against Team Falcons in the Grand Final.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocket_League_Championship_Series#cite_note-19)

The 2026 season started on 14 November 2025 and will end on 20 September 2026. The all new Kickoff Weekend LAN in Copenhagen is happened on 5–7 December and featured the Open 1 top 6 of North America and Europe. 2v2 will also be added to the RLCS.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocket_League_Championship_Series#cite_note-20)

The Kickoff Weekend LAN happened on 5–7 December with the top 6 North American and European teams of Open 1. Their regions Open 1 continued on 5–6 December (Europe on the 5th and North America on the 6th) and the top 4 of each Open advanced to the 8 team stepladder bracket. The winner, Karmine Corp, qualified for the Boston Major and gave Europe an extra qualification spot for the first and second major and the World Championship.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocket_League_Championship_Series#cite_note-:0-1)

The first Major of the season took place in [Boston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston,_Massachusetts "Boston, Massachusetts") at the [Agganis Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agganis_Arena "Agganis Arena") from 19 to 22 February 2026. The qualification process took place from 14 November 2025 to 8 February 2026. The Boston Major consisted of 16 teams in a group stage and an 8 team hybrid elimination playoff bracket.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocket_League_Championship_Series#cite_note-21)

The second Major of the season took place in [Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris "Paris") in the [La Défense Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_La_D%C3%A9fense_Arena "Paris La Défense Arena") from 20 to 24 May 2026. The qualification process took place from 13 March to 26 April 2026. The Paris Major consisted of 16 teams in a group stage and a 12 team hybrid elimination playoff bracket.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocket_League_Championship_Series#cite_note-22)

The Rocket League 2026 World Championship will happen from 15 - 20 September 2026. The Last Chance Qualification stage took place from 2 to 26 July. It will consist of an 8 team GSL play-in bracket, which then takes the top 4 teams and puts them into a group stage with the auto-qualified top 12. From here, the format is the same as the Paris Major. The World Championship will be held at the Dickies Arena in Fort Worth, Texas.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocket_League_Championship_Series#cite_note-23)
